summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Hors 1/34)

data.turoyo: Aṯina bu darbo, kətwaylan ḥa kurmanǧ b qamuṯan, mhalaxwa, saliqina bi kaše, gnəḥtiwayna.
data.translation: Wir waren auf der Straße unterwegs, und vor uns fuhr ein Kurde her. Wir fuhren eine Steigung hinauf und schickten uns an, wieder hinabzufahren.

rationale: Vehicle travel in an ongoing past scene; broad sense 1, with the mode supplied by context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 1.5/43)

data.turoyo: W bat tawfiqat d Aloho ṣafro i naqqa d azzano, malaxlan bu darbayḏan, azole, kəle huwe ste i fadonayḏe, gdowər, kəle barban du darbo, w fayitina aʕle w azzano aḥna b oġur diḏan li qriṯo ḥreto.
data.translation: Und wie es Gott fügte, als wir am Morgen aufbrachen und unseres Weges zogen, da war auch er mit seinem Pfluggespann beim Pflügen, entlang des Weges. Wir zogen an ihm vorüber und gingen auf gut Glück in ein anderes Dorf.

rationale: First-person plural h-less Preterit; retain one representative rather than every reduced token.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (JTM 4.2/10)

rationale: Plural Imperativ fills a cell with three existing examples.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (JTM 5.3/13)

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 5.3/41)

data.translation: Sie machten sich auf, er bestieg den Rücken des Vogels, und sie flogen los.

rationale: Travel on a bird is explicit in the Turoyo; an illustrative participant/mode extension of sense 1.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq Material culture/98)

data.turoyo: Ínaqqa dəmhalxi at+tawre, hano dəgnoḥat bi+arʕo, g̊ḥofar i+arʕo, g̊ḥobašla, g̊sōmla hno hawxa, ǧiwo, gəmhalax bu+ḥaylo dat+tawre, hano u+dworo bu+šəklànoyo.
data.translation: When the bulls move, that one which goes down into the soil, it digs up the soil, it digs it out, it makes it such a whatsit, a furrow, it goes by the strength of the bulls, this is ploughing this way.

rationale: Implement as moving subject and b-marked external force document valency beyond an animate walker.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC MuA Quzko/37)

data.turoyo: Me... me ṣafro hul ʕaṣriye, i+ḥaywanayo lo+rawiʕo, ŭ komalxo, komaləx bəṯra.
data.translation: From the … from the morning until the evening, that animal didn’t lie down, but she walks, he walks behind her.

rationale: One paired feminine/masculine h-less Infectum context replaces multiple repetitive proposals.

summary: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (PrS 24/63)

data.turoyo: Ṣurta d barṯox yo w halxayḏa d barṯox yo, i šġaliyayḏa d barṯox yo.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (26/132)

data.turoyo: D howewo u taǧərawo aṣil, kayiso, i naqqa d məllela hawxa, lazəm d muyadwo u bahro ste quma, maqəṯwo u bahro quma, mhalaxwo aʕma.
data.translation: Wenn der Kaufmann edel gewesen wäre und gut, so hätte er, als er das zu ihr sagte, das Licht (eine Laterne) vor ihr in die Hand nehmen und vor ihr anzünden müssen, und er hätte mit ihr gehen müssen.

rationale: Counterfactual obligation supplies an aspectual contrast, rather than a routine extra walking example.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (46/17)

data.turoyo: Daʕər, maṭʕalle aq qaysayḏe w qləʕle u ḥmorayḏe w malaxle bu darbo.
data.translation: Er kehrte um, lud seine Hölzer auf, trieb seinen Esel an und ging den Weg entlang.

rationale: Clear h-less singular Preterit with overt animate walker and path.

summary: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (57/158)

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (63/45)

data.turoyo: Mhalaxlan qunaġ d yawmo yo aw d tre yo aw d tloṯo yo. Maṭina l ada.
data.translation: Wir fuhren eine Tagereise, oder waren es zwei oder drei, da kamen wir an eine Insel.

rationale: Explicit island endpoint documents sea travel in the existing general movement sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (64/95)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d aṯi u šulṭono w u məǧləsayḏe, ḥəlle: kalayo ḥa rawixo ʕal ḥaṣe du səsyo, w d kətyo kačal, w kalayo ḥa mhalxono. U mhalxono, kəmmat, balki me gawa di bəḥto mofaqlux, ḥaqqaṣ d kətyo zʕuro layəq w šafiro.
data.translation: Als der Sultan und seine Ratsversammlung kamen, sah er: da sitzt einer auf dem Pferd, der ist kahlköpfig, und einer ist zu fuß. Der Fußgänger sieht aus, als ob du ihn aus dem Ei gepellt hättest, ein so hübscher und schmucker Bursche ist er.

rationale: Person-denoting use of mhalxono contrasts with predicative manner use; keep the inherited Nomen Actionis filing pending review.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (71/82)

data.turoyo: Ha i bxeriyayo komhalxo taḥt u qṭoro. Lo qadər nofəq laf larwal.
data.translation: Der Zwischenböden geht unter der Decke entlang; Malke kann nicht hinauskommen.

rationale: Static architectural extent is an unusual participant extension, distinct from physical movement without establishing a separate lexical sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (78/177)

data.turoyo: Annaqla hat gnəḥtət, gəmhalxət halxo, u baytayḏa kale qumux.

rationale: Cognate/manner halxo with a finite verb fills the existing noun cell.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (112/110)

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Talay 1/21)

summary: Routine counts supplied: II Preterit 267, Infectum 124, Imperativ 64, Nomen Actionis 10, Infectum-wa 8. These are additional summarized tokens and need no occurrence decisions.
Walking, riding and crawling are already combined in sense 1. L-series sole movers in the Preterit must remain in that box; semantic intransitivity alone does not create Preterit Intransitive.

Past ongoing or recurrent motion occurs in Infectum-wa; 26/132 is counterfactual obligation. Bare Infectum also supplies movement within past narration. Duration and repetition do not create separate senses.

mhalxono/mhalxone and halxo are BOTH already present, in two Nomen actionis sections. Reject reader claims that halxo or its box is wholly missing; retain the established filing as Nomen Actionis in added labels. 11/97, 71/47 and 75/14 already occur as example or note and are not repeated.
Contracted malax-, malx- forms occur across JTM, Ritter and MAC; retain source spelling. malaxxe can accompany an individual or a group, so no uniform person/number analysis is imposed.
68/24 combines b- manner and aʕmayna for the other party; 21/60 depicts a path outside advice, already quoted. Neither observation requires renumbering sense 1.
MAC NE Keze/14 omits the repeated walking sequence in English; 112/129 renders yawmo as Stunden. Neither is selected as a bilingual example.
Batch 2 preserves all batch-1 decisions and examples. New 1a concerns success of a matter and does not overturn the participant-extension treatment of customs and practices.
Motor travel now has a vehicle-subject example; the remaining repeated reduced Preterit proposals add no unrepresented form. 115/52 and 115/92 juxtapose reduced and full forms within one verse.
No secure new collocation is shown. halax (113/180) remains ambiguous between a bleached command and a particle; gəmhaxli (115/154) and -anne (115/92) remain source/morphology questions.
Do editors wish to distinguish agreement-bearing mhalxono/mhalxone from halxo within the two inherited Nomen Actionis sections? No new Infinitiv is established.
Is halux in 95/95, 112, 116, 118; 97/40; 98/18; 109/4 a verb variant of haləx or a presentative directive? These analyses remain provisional and no example is added.

Check mhalaxe (69/507), mhalaxla with a masculine traveller (70/30), Gəmhaxli/mhaxli/komhaxli (73/117, 294; 79/12), hat mhalxo (81/118), and mhalaxxena (98/9) against the editions or recordings; no spelling correction is invented.
Does halexunne (96/164) lexicalize attack or simply direct motion to a hostile destination? Confirm the suffix's function.
Can the omitted motion clauses at MAC NE Keze/14 and day/hour mismatch at 112/129 be checked in the editions?
Confirm the single success/functioning attestation at 115/171 and whether 1a should ultimately be a full numbered sense.
Check Halax (113/180), -anne (115/92), and printed gəmhaxli (115/154) against source or speaker before treating them as distinct verbal forms.

summary: Motor, sea and airborne travel change the mode of movement, not the lexical meaning.

Abstract custom/practice as understood subject, conduct of a council, construction progress, moving plough and fixed architectural extent extend participants or path construal; they do not establish separate senses here.
Talay alternates driver, passengers and vehicle as sole participant of motor travel. m- can mark the village left behind; emigration is the discourse setting, not a new lexical meaning.
